applied.quote: At ModernWallet, we wrote this guide from the federal courts' [Chapter 7 rules](https://www.uscourts.gov/court-programs/bankruptcy/bankruptcy-basics/chapter-7-bankruptcy-basics) and the Bankruptcy Code text, so each step below carries its own deadline.
applied.replacement: At The Modern Wallet, we wrote this guide from the federal courts' [Chapter 7 rules](https://www.uscourts.gov/court-programs/bankruptcy/bankruptcy-basics/chapter-7-bankruptcy-basics) and the Bankruptcy Code text.
applied.why: Site is named The Modern Wallet; steps 3 and 5 carry no deadline.

applied.quote: One course must happen before you file and a second course after, or the court closes the case without wiping out any debt.
applied.replacement: One course must happen before you file and a second course after, and without the second, the clerk closes the case without a discharge.
applied.why: Closing without discharge applies to a missing debtor-education certificate, not to counseling.

applied.quote: The debtor education certificate is the step people can miss after the hard part is over.
applied.replacement: The debtor education certificate is a separate requirement after filing.
applied.why: SOURCE says nothing about what people typically miss.

applied.quote: The most recent federal figure is a [Government Accountability Office study](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-08-697) estimating the average fee rose from $712 in early 2005 to $1,078 in early 2007.
applied.replacement: A 2008 [Government Accountability Office study](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-08-697) estimated the average fee rose from $712 in early 2005 to $1,078 in early 2007.
applied.why: SOURCE does not say GAO is the most recent federal figure.

applied.quote: The two required courses add less.
applied.replacement: The two required courses carry their own fees.
applied.why: SOURCE makes no comparison of course costs to attorney fees.

applied.quote: Money in your accounts is property you list on Schedule A/B, and Chapter 7 sells nonexempt property to pay creditors, so what you keep depends on the exemptions you claim on Schedule C.
applied.replacement: You list all your property on Schedule A/B, and Chapter 7 sells nonexempt property to pay creditors, so what you keep depends on the exemptions you claim on Schedule C.
applied.why: SOURCE never says bank balances go on Schedule A/B.

applied.quote: Emptying an account to pay one creditor before filing can backfire, since the trustee can set aside many payments made in the last 90 days.
applied.replacement: Paying one creditor before filing also matters, since the trustee can set aside certain payments to creditors made in the 90 days before filing.
applied.why: "Backfire" and "many payments" overstate; §547 has insolvency and other conditions.

applied.quote: It usually refers to two rules.
applied.replacement: Two Chapter 7 rules use a 90-day window.
applied.why: SOURCE says nothing about what the phrase usually refers to.

applied.quote: Chapter 7 leaves certain taxes, domestic support, most student loans, government fines, criminal restitution and debts from intoxicated driving in place.
applied.replacement: Chapter 7 leaves certain taxes, domestic support, student loans unless repaying them would impose an undue hardship, government fines, criminal restitution and debts from intoxicated driving in place.
applied.why: SOURCE says student loans survive unless undue hardship; no "most".

applied.quote: Creditors and the trustee have 60 days after the first date set for the 341 meeting to file a complaint objecting to your discharge.
applied.replacement: A complaint objecting to your discharge must be filed within 60 days after the first date set for the 341 meeting.
applied.why: Rule 4004(a)(1) sets the 60-day deadline; SOURCE does not name who may file.

applied.quote: The two required courses carry their own fees.
applied.replacement: Approved providers of the two required courses may charge a fee.
applied.why: SOURCE says providers may charge a fee; courses can also be free.
